title: Probe posts: report the measured deviation on the control (e.g. PathPilot DEBUG) before writing the offset

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Asked by the contributor after #521's hands-on probe run on a real Tormach 770MX, 2026-11-09: "did the probe report any issues or changes from expected? If so, where/how?"

**Today:** a probing program is silent when it succeeds. It stores the trip point (`#100..`), computes the error (`#190=[#102-0]`), stops with a message only when the error is out of tolerance (`(MSG, PROBE Z OUT OF TOLERANCE)` + `M2`), and otherwise rewrites the work offset with `G10 L20` without a word.
- **On the 770MX:** G54 Z moved from -8.3252 to -8.3259 (the top read 0.0007 in low). The offset table was the only trace, and the operator could not tell from the screen what the probe measured or what it changed.

**Expected:** before the offset write, the post reports the measured deviation per probed axis on the control's operator-message channel. The program does not stop for it.
- **Tormach/LinuxCNC:** `(DEBUG, PROBE Z ERROR #190)`. PathPilot shows DEBUG lines in its status log with the parameter's value substituted.
- **Other dialects:** each one's non-stopping message equivalent where it has one (e.g. Haas/Fanuc macro `#3006` stops, so not that one; a dialect with no non-stopping message says so in the post and is skipped).
- A probe op that sets no work offset (measure only) reports the same way, since then the message is the whole output.

**Done means:** the Tormach post emits one report line per probed axis, after the tolerance check and before `G10`, and a golden or test pins its text and position. Other dialects either emit their equivalent or are recorded as having none (decision file). A cutting op's output is unchanged.

Related: #362 / PR #521 (Tormach probing hooks), #522, #570, #574.
